big-news.text: PST says a terror attempt in Norway next year is "likely." The threat level stays at 3 of 5, and PST has added a new category, "nihilistic extremism," for violent online networks.
Equinor is dealing with an ongoing cyberattack that has disrupted some IT systems. It says oil and gas production isn't affected and there's no sign data was stolen.

whats-changing.text: Experts say southern Norway could see its priciest winter ever for power, close to 2 kr/kWh on average before grid fees. Norgespris shields you from that.
Helsedirektoratet (the health directorate) and FHI say to keep the ban on drinking in public parks. Stortinget could still let cities set up drinking zones if Ap backs the idea.

oslo.text: The T-bane shutdown starts TOMORROW and runs Thursday to Sunday. No metro runs through the city centre, lines 4 and 5 are fully closed, and lines 1 to 3 only run short stretches in the west. Use tram 19x (Majorstuen to Stortorvet) or buses 2B, 3B or 25B.
A new analysis says Fornebubanen could cost up to 34.8 billion kr, 7.3 billion over the original target, and the opposition is already warning of higher tolls.

be-aware.text: Taxis and Bolt will be swamped during the shutdown. Oslo Taxi may run out of cars and Bolt uses surge pricing, so book early. Car sharing or a bike is a good backup.
Asker found fake EasyPark QR stickers on parking machines that lead to a fake payment page. Always pay in the app, never through a sticker.
It'll be cold and dry, from about −5° to +3° through the weekend, so watch for icy patches in the mornings.

fun-and-free.text: Top pick: The free Christmas light-up at Sommerro is tonight at 16:45.
Åges Danseband plays a free show at Proud Mary tonight at 21:30 (age 20+).
Jul i Vinterland in Spikersuppa is free, with gløgg, a Ferris wheel and concerts. It's within walking distance of most places this weekend.
The Botanisk hage Christmas market is on Saturday from 11:00 to 16:00, with crafts, waffles and a choir at 12:00. There's no T-bane to Tøyen that day.
